harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster on CentOS Stream 10 (via EPEL erlang-repo substitution since el10 packages weren't yet published, using el9 RPMs which are ABI-compatible). Created a `payments` vhost with default queue type quorum, an `app_user` account with full permissions scoped to that vhost, and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all 3 nodes. Demonstrated that durable messages survive the loss of any one node (stopped the queue leader node1, verified quorum queue re-elected a leader on node2 and all 3 messages remained consumable from a surviving node), then restored node1 and confirmed full cluster health. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time native reboot protocol for all three nodes, verifying changed boot_id and full RabbitMQ/cluster/quorum-queue recovery after each restart, finishing with an end-to-end publish/consume check confirming the app account and queue are fully functional with no alarms or partitions.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes: fresh CentOS Stream 10, no RabbitMQ/Erlang installed
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes
Installed epel-release; found no el10 erlang/rabbitmq packages in stock repos
Configured packagecloud.io rabbitmq/erlang and rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server repos, rewrote baseurl from el/10 to el/9 (only published version) on all 3 nodes
Installed erlang 26.2.5.4 and rabbitmq-server 3.13.7 on all 3 nodes
Started and enabled rabbitmq-server on all 3 nodes
Synced Erlang cookie across all 3 nodes for clustering
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 25672, 5672, 15672, 35672-35682 on all 3 nodes (were blocking inter-node Erlang distribution)
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3-node disk cluster
Created 'payments' vhost with --default-queue-type quorum
Generated a random app_user password on-node via openssl and passed it through secret_env; created app_user with full permissions on payments vhost and management tag
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and rabbitmqadmin CLI on all 3 nodes
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' (3 members: node1, node2, node3)
Published 3 durable test messages, confirmed queue depth
Captured healthy baseline, then stopped rabbitmq-server on the queue leader (node1) to simulate node loss
Verified from node2 that cluster kept quorum, queue re-elected leader on node2, all 3 messages intact and consumable; consumed all 3 messages successfully from a surviving node
Restarted node1's rabbitmq-server and verified full cluster/queue recovery (3 members, no data loss)
Published 3 more baseline durable messages for the restart protocol
Captured OS boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, node2, node3 (one at a time) via systemctl reboot with backgrounded/disowned command so ack returned pre-disconnect
Polled each node until reachable again and confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart
Verified after each single-node restart: rabbitmq-server active, all 3 nodes in cluster_status Running Nodes, quorum queue 'orders' back to 3 members with all messages retained, no alarms/partitions
Final end-to-end check: published and consumed a post-restart message via app_user credentials confirming full functionality

evidence.summary: join_cluster output and cluster_status show rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes after joining node2 and node3 to node1

evidence.requirement: payments vhost created with app account able to publish/consume
evidence.summary: payments vhost created with default_queue_type=quorum; app_user created and granted full (.*, .*, .*) permissions on payments; app_user successfully declared queue and published messages via rabbitmqadmin

evidence.requirement: Durable queue replicated across nodes for HA
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl list_queues shows quorum queue 'orders' with members [rabbit@node1, rabbit@node3, rabbit@node2] -- full 3-way replication

evidence.requirement: Messages survive loss of any one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: 3 durable messages published and confirmed (messages=3); node1 (queue leader) stopped; from node2, cluster_status shows only node2/node3 running yet queue re-elected leader=rabbit@node2 with messages=3 intact; all 3 messages successfully consumed (get) from surviving node2 while node1 was down

evidence.requirement: Cluster/queue recovers fully after disrupted node returns
evidence.summary: node1 restarted and rejoined; cluster_status shows all 3 Running Nodes, no alarms/partitions; queue back to 3 members; fresh baseline messages published and confirmed

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id fb2aa416... captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect (subsequent call got connection reset); polling succeeded once boot_id read as 91e27822... (changed); rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status/list_queues show all 3 nodes running and quorum queue with 3 members and 3 messages restored

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d052eb57... captured; reboot acknowledged then connection reset; boot_id after recovery is 3d9c387e... (changed); rabbitmq-server active; cluster_status confirms all 3 nodes Running; quorum queue members=3, messages=3

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f7db4b4e... captured; reboot acknowledged then connection reset; boot_id after recovery is 2e19292d... (changed); rabbitmq-server active; cluster_status confirms all 3 nodes Running; quorum queue members=3, messages=3

evidence.requirement: Final post-restart functional verification, no alarms/partitions
evidence.summary: New durable message published and all 4 messages (3 baseline + 1 post-restart) successfully retrieved via app_user; cluster_status shows Alarms: (none), Network Partitions: (none)
